findings.title: Wire the accepted timeout into the shutdown drain
findings.problem: Setting [general].shutdown_drain_timeout = 120.5 is now accepted and preserved by the model, but with no environment override the scheduler still selects the hardcoded 60.0 default (triggarr/search/scheduler.py:70–81). Shutdown uses that constant at line 634 and closes resources after expiry, ignoring the configured drain budget. The TOML loading path in triggarr/config.py:load_settings exposes this setting now; this is more than an unused internal field.

members.title: Saving settings silently resets a configured shutdown_drain_timeout to 60.0
members.problem: The diff adds shutdown_drain_timeout to GeneralConfig as a persisted config field. The POST /settings handler (triggarr/web/routes.py:539-551) rebuilds the whole `general` dict from form fields only. It does not include shutdown_drain_timeout, and it does not carry the field over from current_settings the way it does for tracking_delay_seconds at line 547. Suppose someone sets shutdown_drain_timeout in the TOML by hand. The next settings save validates the general config without that key, so it falls back to the default of 60.0 and the user's value is overwritten without warning. The field comment mentions a 'form clamp (3600.0)', but no form input or clamp exists in routes.py or settings.html. pending: confirm that a later plan in this phase adds the form field or a carry-over before this change ships on its own.

members.title: New config field has no consumer, so the scheduler still ignores it
members.problem: The scheduler still uses the module-level _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT. That constant is read once at import time from the env var only (triggarr/search/scheduler.py:58-81, used at 611-656). Nothing reads settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout. The field comment says 'Config value is the default; env overrides', but in this state a TOML value is validated and then has no effect. This is a staged change (the spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-recovery-counts-config-design.md:175 plans the wiring), so on its own it is not proven to be a defect. pending: confirm the scheduler wiring lands in the same release.

members.title: No upper bound, so a config value can exceed the Docker stop grace period
members.problem: The model sets ge=1.0 and blocks inf/nan, but it has no `le` bound. A finite value such as 1e9 in the TOML is accepted. docker-compose.yml:24 and README.md:86 say the drain must stay below stop_grace_period (90s). Without that limit, Docker sends SIGKILL in the middle of the drain. The only ceiling is the 3600.0 'form clamp' named in the comment, which does not exist yet and would not apply to TOML edits anyway. This change only tightens validation, so it is capped. pending: confirm whether a model-level ceiling is wanted.
